title: Senior's toolkit: TCP and MTU on a live system
summary: Read round-trip times, retransmits and socket states from ss, catch resets in tcpdump, and find an MTU black hole.

steps.title: Senior's toolkit: TCP and MTU on a live system
steps.body: When a transfer is slow or connections pile up, the kernel already knows why: RTT, retransmits, window sizes and socket states. These commands read it out.

toolkit.what: Per-connection TCP internals: round-trip time, congestion window and retransmit counts. Shows whether a slow transfer is loss, latency or a small window.
flags: current / total retransmits: a rising total means loss
toolkit.when: a download is slow and bandwidth looks fine

toolkit.what: One-screen summary of all sockets by state. Thousands in `timewait` or `estab` point to connection churn or a leak.
Lists sockets in one TCP state. Counting them by peer shows which client opens a new connection per request instead of reusing one.
toolkit.example: ss -tan state close-wait | awk 'NR>1 {print $4}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head

toolkit.what: Captures only SYNs and resets. Shows unanswered SYNs (a firewall drops them) and who sends the RST that kills connections.
Sends a full 1500-byte packet with Don't Fragment set. If it fails while smaller ones pass, something on the path has a smaller MTU, for example a VPN or tunnel.
flags: set Don't Fragment, never fragment locally
finds the path MTU hop by hop, no root needed
toolkit.when: small requests work but large responses or TLS handshakes hang

toolkit.cmd: ip link set dev wg0 mtu 1380
toolkit.what: Lowers an interface MTU so packets fit through the narrowest link. The usual fix for a tunnel black hole, alongside MSS clamping on the gateway.
Sends UDP data by hand. UDP has no handshake, so "no error" proves nothing; watch for the reply, or run tcpdump on the receiver.
flags: listen for UDP on the other side to test both ends

steps.prompt: Match each observation to what it points to.
pairs: the app never closes connections the peer already closed
Many SYNs in tcpdump, no SYN-ACK
a firewall drops the connection attempts
a link on the path has a smaller MTU
a new connection per request instead of reuse

steps.prompt: Over the new site-to-site VPN, `curl` to an internal API returns small JSON fine, but downloading a 2 MB report hangs forever. `ping` works. What do you test next?
options: `ping -M do -s 1472` to the API, then smaller sizes, to look for an MTU black hole
steps.explain: Small packets fit, full-size ones are dropped, and the ICMP "fragmentation needed" message is blocked somewhere, so TCP never learns to send smaller segments. Fix it with a lower tunnel MTU or MSS clamping.

steps.prompt: An API server starts failing with `too many open files`. `ss -s` shows 28,000 TCP sockets, and `ss -tan state close-wait | wc -l` prints 27,500. Where is the bug?
options: In the app: it does not close sockets after the peer hangs up (for example an HTTP response or DB connection never disposed)
In the network: packets are lost
The client keeps the connection open too long
The kernel's TIME_WAIT timer is too long
steps.explain: CLOSE_WAIT means the other side sent FIN and the local application has not called close. Only the app can leave that state, so the leak is in its code.

steps.prompt: Show TCP internals (RTT, retransmits) for every connection to port 443.
steps.explain: `-t` TCP and `-i` internal info. `dport` filters on the remote port of outgoing connections; `sport` would be your own listening port.

steps.title: Make it a habit
steps.body: When something is slow or connections pile up, look at `ss -s` and `ss -ti` before you change timeouts: they say whether the cause is loss, latency or the app. Any time a tunnel or VPN is involved and big transfers hang, test the MTU first.
